₹25 lakh per category, and just two days left to apply.

The National Startup Awards 6.0 from DPIIT's Startup India close on 20 November. This edition is far bigger than the last one: the winner in each of 20 sector categories, plus Women-Led Startup of the Year and North-East Startup Excellence, takes home ₹25 lakh, up from ₹10 lakh last time. There is also a separate pool for school and college student innovators, with prizes from ₹2 lakh to ₹6 lakh.

Beyond the cash, winners get mentoring, investor and corporate connects, market access, and priority visibility at DPIIT-backed startup events in India and abroad. No equity is taken.

You can apply if you are a DPIIT-recognised private limited company, LLP or registered partnership, not more than 10 years old, and your turnover has never crossed ₹100 crore in any financial year. Past NSA winners cannot re-apply, and the student track does not need DPIIT recognition.

The tip founders miss: keep your DPIIT certificate and recent financial statements ready before you open the form, and read the category rules carefully so you enter where your impact numbers are strongest. Do not wait for a last-minute extension.

What if 3 to 6 global banks were assigned to mentor your fintech startup, for free and with zero equity?

That is the FinTech Innovation Lab New York, run by the Partnership Fund for New York City with Accenture, and applications for the 2027 class close on 25 November. It is a 12-week hybrid programme from March to June 2027 that pairs B2B fintech startups with senior executives from three to six of its 40-plus participating banks, insurers and asset managers. Each pairing comes with an executive sponsor and a day-to-day contact, and a typical cohort of about ten companies starts 20 to 40 proofs of concept. Growth-stage companies can also join a Pilot Track with Accenture's Innovation Garage.

It is open to early- and growth-stage companies, usually pre-seed to Series B, with at least a beta product, and non-US startups, including Indian ones, can apply.

The catch founders overlook: the Lab does not sponsor visas or reimburse travel, and your core team must attend in-person sessions in New York. Plan your visa and budget before you apply. Since the deadline is in US time, submit by the evening of 24 November IST.

Agritech founders: there is a ₹25 lakh government grant open right now, and you do not need to move to the North-East to get it.

NEATEHUB in Jorhat, Assam, has opened Cohort 13 of its RKVY-RAFTAAR Saranya programme, funded under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. Selected startups receive up to ₹25 lakh as grant-in-aid with no equity taken, released in three milestone-linked tranches over 12 to 18 months. Alongside the money come go-to-market mentorship, technical guidance and access to follow-on investor networks. The programme is non-residential; you only travel to Jorhat for the committee pitch and the valedictory session.

It is meant for DPIIT-recognised agri and allied-sector startups under seven years old with a working MVP or pilot that has real users and data. The majority of equity must be held by Indian citizens, and OCI founders qualify. Revenue-generating startups, ideally at ₹10 lakh ARR or more, fit best, and pure trading or service businesses without an innovation core are excluded.

Practical tip: applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so applying in the first half of the window genuinely helps. Pilots in North-East India earn extra points but are not mandatory.
